network.overall_strategy: Surface-dominated, acetaldehyde-centered network. Three experimentally grounded threonine families are represented: (i) glycine and oligoglycine capture of acetaldehyde in warm acidic waters, (ii) the cyanosulfidic sequence acetaldehyde -> lactonitrile -> lactaldehyde -> threonine aminonitrile -> threonine, and (iii) aminomalononitrile capture of acetaldehyde followed by hydrolysis/decarboxylation. Alternative Cu-assisted versus Cu-free photoredox and neutral versus acidic aminonitrile hydrolysis are separated as distinct branches. To keep the graph conservation-valid, unresolved radiolysis, discharge, and ice-residue routes are not encoded as single black-box edges, and composite workup nodes are written with explicit water, ammonia, and CO2 bookkeeping. Hot hydrothermal production is not favored because the target-specific literature is stronger for surface and concentrated-pool chemistry.

reactions.name: Direct glycine-acetaldehyde condensation to threonine

conditions.other: Weakly acidic homogeneous solution, pH 3.3-3.7, 60-80 C, no inorganic solids

reactions.mechanism: Net reverse-retro-aldol or imine-enamine aldol-type C-C bond formation between glycine and acetaldehyde gives the beta-hydroxy-alpha-amino acid skeleton.
reactions.reasoning: Ivanov and Ivanov reported threonine among products from glycine plus acetaldehyde under weakly acidic warm aqueous conditions without inorganic solids (Ivanov & Ivanov, 1983). Formaldehyde was also present in the original mixtures, but it is omitted here because acetaldehyde provides the threonine-specific methyl-bearing carbon unit. The reaction is experimentally grounded but poorly selective and in reality gives a threonine/allothreonine family rather than a single stereoisomer.

reactions.name: Diglycine-assisted acetaldehyde conversion to threonine

conditions.other: Weakly acidic homogeneous solution, pH 3.3-3.7, 60-80 C, peptide-rich pool, no inorganic solids

reactions.mechanism: An oligoglycine residue captures acetaldehyde and undergoes rearrangement or hydrolytic chain-shortening, releasing one glycine equivalent while generating the threonine skeleton.
reactions.reasoning: Ivanov and Ivanov explicitly used glycine oligohomopeptides as substrates and observed threonine among products under the same weakly acidic warm aqueous conditions (Ivanov & Ivanov, 1983). The exact microscopic sequence was not resolved, so this is a balanced net representation of oligoglycine-assisted threonine formation rather than a claimed single elementary step. As with the monomer route, the real product distribution is broad and includes non-target amino acids.

reactions.name: Triglycine-assisted acetaldehyde conversion to threonine

conditions.other: Weakly acidic homogeneous solution, pH 3.3-3.7, 60-80 C, peptide-rich pool, no inorganic solids

reactions.mechanism: A longer oligoglycine chain mediates acetaldehyde incorporation into a beta-hydroxy-alpha-amino-acid product while the residual peptide shortens by one glycine unit.
reactions.reasoning: The oligoglycine experiments of Ivanov and Ivanov support threonine formation from glycine homopeptides plus acetaldehyde under primitive-earth-like acidic warm aqueous conditions (Ivanov & Ivanov, 1983). This triglycine node is a route-class abstraction consistent with those experiments, not a fully resolved elementary mechanism. It is included because the paper specifically showed that oligoglycine substrates can channel carbon into threonine-family products.

reactions.name: Acetaldehyde cyanohydrin formation

conditions.other: Near-neutral cyanide-rich surface water; cyanohydrin capture of acetaldehyde

reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of cyanide to acetaldehyde gives the cyanohydrin lactonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Acetaldehyde capture by HCN to form lactonitrile is the entry point to the mechanistically explicit threonine branch developed in the cyanosulfidic literature (Ritson & Sutherland, 2013; Patel et al., 2015). This is straightforward cyanohydrin chemistry and is one of the best-defined upstream steps in the threonine network.

reactions.name: CuCN-assisted H2S photoreduction of lactonitrile to lactaldehyde

conditions.other: 254 nm UV, near-neutral pH around 7, phosphate present, H2S as stoichiometric reductant

reactions.mechanism: UV-driven Cu(I)/sulfide photoredox reduces the nitrile carbon to the aldehyde level with hydrolytic ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: Ritson and Sutherland measured conversion of the acetaldehyde-cyanohydrin system to lactaldehyde in 19% yield under UV irradiation with H2S, phosphate, and CuCN at near-neutral pH, and Patel et al. placed this step in a broader cyanosulfidic network (Ritson & Sutherland, 2013; Patel et al., 2015). Cu(I) is therefore treated here as a demonstrated accelerator. Elemental sulfur is written as the minimal redox-bookkeeping sink for oxidized sulfide; real sulfur speciation may be more complex.

reactions.name: Cu-free H2S photoreduction of lactonitrile to lactaldehyde

conditions.other: 254 nm UV, near-neutral pH, H2S-rich Cu-free photoredox variant

reactions.mechanism: UV-excited sulfide provides reductive power for nitrile-to-aldehyde conversion without invoking Cu(I) as an obligatory catalyst.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. argued that H2S-containing homologation chemistry is not absolutely dependent on Cu(I), and Xu et al. later showed that alternative photoredox systems can drive related HCN reductive homologations (Patel et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2018). This Cu-free branch is therefore chemically justified, but it is less directly demonstrated for the specific lactonitrile-to-lactaldehyde threonine branch than the CuCN-assisted implementation of Ritson and Sutherland. Sulfur is again a simplified redox-bookkeeping product.

reactions.name: Strecker conversion of lactaldehyde to threonine aminonitrile

conditions.other: Near-neutral aqueous HCN and excess NH3; timescale days to weeks

reactions.mechanism: Lactaldehyde undergoes imine formation with ammonia, cyanide capture, and aminonitrile stabilization to give the threonine-family Strecker precursor.
reactions.reasoning: Ritson and Sutherland showed that lactaldehyde, after HCN addition and exposure to excess NH3, proceeds to the threonine/allo-threonine Strecker aminonitrile rather than directly to free threonine (Ritson & Sutherland, 2013). This node keeps that precursor-level realism and avoids overstating free-threonine accumulation.

reactions.name: Neutral aqueous hydrolysis of threonine aminonitrile

conditions.other: Long residence time in neutral to mildly acidic pools or geothermal cycling

reactions.mechanism: Stepwise nitrile hydration and hydrolysis convert the aminonitrile carbon into the carboxyl group of threonine, releasing ammonia overall.
reactions.reasoning: Environmental hydrolysis of the threonine aminonitrile is chemically required to reach free threonine, but the supplied literature mainly emphasizes aminonitrile or residue precursors and often uses strong analytical hydrolysis for final detection. This neutral-water version is therefore plausible but kinetically uncertain and should be regarded as a slower, partly speculative completion step anchored by the precursor chemistry of Ritson and Sutherland (2013).

reactions.name: Acid-accelerated hydrolysis of threonine aminonitrile

conditions.other: Acidic pool or hot-spring margin; faster hydrolysis than neutral water

reactions.mechanism: Acid-promoted nitrile hydration and hydrolysis accelerate conversion of the aminonitrile to the amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Acidic aqueous hydrolysis is more consistent with how threonine is commonly released from aminonitrile-like or residue-bound precursors in experimental work, even though laboratory protocols are often harsher than any single natural setting (Thanassi, 1975; Sweeney et al., 1976; Elsila et al., 2007). This node is included as a geochemically milder analogue of that hydrolytic release and remains less directly demonstrated than aminonitrile formation itself.

reactions.name: Aminomalononitrile capture of acetaldehyde followed by hydrolysis and decarboxylation

conditions.other: Composite net step: near-neutral AMN addition to acetaldehyde, then acidic hydrolysis and decarboxylation

reactions.mechanism: Aminomalononitrile adds to acetaldehyde to give a beta-hydroxy dinitrile adduct; subsequent nitrile hydrolysis yields a dicarboxylate precursor that decarboxylates to threonine.
reactions.reasoning: Thanassi reported D,L-threonine and allo-threonine from aminomalononitrile plus acetaldehyde after hydrolysis and decarboxylation, and Kuroda et al. later summarized this as near-neutral aqueous alkylation followed by acidic workup (Thanassi, 1975; Kuroda et al., 2020). The node is intentionally encoded as a composite net transformation because the experimentally decisive endpoint is free threonine after hydrolysis rather than an isolated environmental adduct.

reactions.name: Wet-dry condensation of glycine to diglycine

conditions.other: Dehydrating wet-dry cycles in concentrated amino-acid films or pools

reactions.mechanism: Dehydrative peptide-bond formation couples two glycine molecules to give diglycine.
reactions.reasoning: Ivanov and Ivanov used oligoglycine substrates in threonine-forming experiments, so including diglycine as an in-network precursor is chemically useful (Ivanov & Ivanov, 1983). The peptide-formation step itself is not a threonine-specific result from the supplied corpus; it is a standard prebiotic-pool assumption introduced to represent those experimentally used oligohomopeptides and is consistent with older peptide-like material from cyanide chemistry (Lowe et al., 1963; Matthews & Moser, 1967).

reactions.name: Wet-dry elongation of diglycine to triglycine

conditions.other: Dehydrating wet-dry cycles in concentrated peptide-rich pools

reactions.mechanism: Further dehydrative peptide-bond formation extends diglycine by one glycine unit to triglycine.
reactions.reasoning: Triglycine extends the same oligoglycine logic used experimentally by Ivanov and Ivanov (Ivanov & Ivanov, 1983). As with rxn_011, the elongation step itself is a chemically plausible but partly speculative prebiotic-pool assumption introduced to represent oligohomopeptide substrates rather than a directly measured threonine-specific elementary reaction.

pathways.name: Direct glycine-acetaldehyde condensation
pathways.description: Catalyst-free warm acidic aqueous conversion of glycine and acetaldehyde directly into the threonine family.

pathways.name: Glycine via diglycine-assisted condensation
pathways.description: Glycine first condenses to diglycine in a dehydrating pool; diglycine then reacts with acetaldehyde and water to release threonine plus glycine.

pathways.name: Glycine via triglycine-assisted condensation
pathways.description: A longer oligoglycine ladder is built before acetaldehyde capture generates threonine and shortens the peptide.

pathways.name: Entry from pre-existing diglycine pools
pathways.description: If diglycine has already accumulated in peptide-rich prebiotic pools, it can directly channel acetaldehyde into threonine.

pathways.name: Entry from pre-existing triglycine pools
pathways.description: If triglycine is already present, acetaldehyde capture yields threonine while shortening the peptide to diglycine.

pathways.name: Cu-assisted cyanosulfidic Strecker with neutral hydrolysis
pathways.description: Acetaldehyde is trapped as lactonitrile, photoreduced to lactaldehyde under CuCN/H2S/UV conditions, converted to threonine aminonitrile, then hydrolyzed slowly in water.

pathways.name: Cu-assisted cyanosulfidic Strecker with acidic hydrolysis
pathways.description: The same Cu-assisted cyanosulfidic precursor sequence is completed in a warmer acidic pool where aminonitrile hydrolysis is faster.

pathways.name: Cu-free cyanosulfidic Strecker with neutral hydrolysis
pathways.description: A Cu-free H2S/UV variant of the photoredox reduction supplies lactaldehyde, followed by Strecker aminonitrile formation and slower neutral hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Cu-free cyanosulfidic Strecker with acidic hydrolysis
pathways.description: The Cu-free photoredox branch converges on threonine aminonitrile and is completed in an acidic aqueous setting.

pathways.name: Aminomalononitrile-acetaldehyde route
pathways.description: Aminomalononitrile captures acetaldehyde and, after hydrolysis and decarboxylation, yields threonine directly as a net transformation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Good literature-aligned net edge for the Ivanov & Ivanov 1983 weakly acidic aqueous route. Chemistry is plausible if Surface means warm acidic surface water, but the single edge hides low selectivity and likely threonine/allothreonine mixtures.
suggestions: Add explicit pH 3.3-3.7 and 60-80 C conditions to rxn_001.
Annotate that the route is low-selectivity and likely yields threonine plus allothreonine and other amino acids.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reasonable extension of the Ivanov oligoglycine chemistry, but rxn_011 is only balanceable as 2 glycine -> diglycine + water and the Biochemical label is not the right prebiotic setting for wet-dry peptide formation. Transfer from that label to Surface is not justified as written.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_011 as 2 mol_004 -> mol_005 + mol_003.
Replace the Biochemical label with a nonenzymatic wet-dry surface setting.
Add acidic aqueous conditions for rxn_002 and note mixed-product output.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically plausible as a peptide-assisted Ivanov variant, but the route depends on two nonenzymatic peptide-condensation steps mislabeled as Biochemical. The triglycine-assisted step is acceptable as a net transformation, yet selectivity and environmental continuity are under-specified.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_011 as 2 mol_004 -> mol_005 + mol_003.
Relabel rxn_011 and rxn_012 as nonenzymatic wet-dry surface chemistry.
Add concentration and temperature assumptions for oligoglycine buildup.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strong oligoglycine entry as encoded, assuming a pre-existing diglycine pool. This matches the Ivanov & Ivanov 1983 observations, though the route remains low-selectivity and should be treated as producing threonine-family mixtures rather than a clean single product.
suggestions: Add weakly acidic aqueous conditions for rxn_002.
Annotate low selectivity and expected threonine/allothreonine mixtures.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Acceptable pre-existing triglycine entry to the Ivanov oligoglycine branch. The net stoichiometry is fine, but the route still lacks explicit pH/temperature detail and probably yields broad amino-acid mixtures.
suggestions: Add weakly acidic aqueous conditions for rxn_003.
Annotate low selectivity and expected mixed amino-acid products.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The upstream sequence is very well aligned with Ritson & Sutherland 2013 and Patel et al. 2015: acetaldehyde -> lactonitrile -> lactaldehyde -> threonine aminonitrile. The weak point is rxn_008: it is only balanceable as mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002, neutral aminonitrile hydrolysis is kinetically slow, and labeling it Biochemical is not a realistic prebiotic environment.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_008 as mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002.
Replace Biochemical with a defined neutral aqueous environment and a realistic time scale.
Consider ending the pathway at threonine aminonitrile unless hydrolysis data are supplied.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best mechanistically defined pathway in the network. The cyanosulfidic/Strecker sequence is strongly literature-grounded by Ritson & Sutherland 2013 and Patel et al. 2015, and acidic hydrolysis is more credible than the neutral branch. Remaining caveats are that rxn_009 needs explicit stoichiometry, mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002, and the literature is stronger for aminonitrile formation than for environmentally realistic free-threonine release.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_009 as mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002.
Specify UV, pH, CuCN, and H2S conditions for the photoredox step and separate them from the acidic hydrolysis setting.
Annotate threonine/allothreonine output rather than a single stereochemically silent threonine node.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Coherent route, but weaker than the Cu-assisted branch. Cu-free sulfide photoreduction is plausible in the broader cyanosulfidic literature, yet the threonine-specific implementation is less directly established, and the same neutral-hydrolysis problem remains at rxn_008.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_008 as mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002.
Give explicit Cu-free photoredox conditions and justify them from the literature.
Consider stopping the path at threonine aminonitrile if neutral hydrolysis remains unsupported.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reasonable alternative to the Cu-assisted path, with a chemically sensible acidic hydrolysis endpoint. It is still weaker than P7 because the Cu-free lactonitrile-to-lactaldehyde step is less directly anchored in the threonine-specific literature and rxn_009 remains under-specified stoichiometrically.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_009 as mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002.
State the Cu-free photoredox evidence and conditions more explicitly.
Annotate sulfide/UV geochemical constraints and threonine/allothreonine output.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This matches the Thanassi 1975 aminomalononitrile + acetaldehyde family and is one of the better direct threonine routes in the literature. The main issue is granularity: rxn_010 collapses C-C addition, hydrolysis, and decarboxylation into one Surface step and is only balanceable as mol_013 + mol_007 + 4 mol_003 -> mol_015 + 2 mol_002 + mol_014.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_010 as mol_013 + mol_007 + 4 mol_003 -> mol_015 + 2 mol_002 + mol_014.
Split the acetaldehyde addition from hydrolysis/decarboxylation into separate nodes.
Specify near-neutral addition conditions followed by the acidic hydrolysis/decarboxylation regime.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected, literature-aware network with no RDKit-flagged UNBALANCED reactions; four edges are only balanceable with implicit coefficients. It captures the three strongest target-specific terrestrial families: Ivanov glycine/oligoglycine chemistry, the Ritson-Sutherland lactaldehyde/Strecker branch, and the Thanassi aminomalononitrile branch, and it sensibly avoids black-box discharge, radiolysis, and ice edges. The choice not to prioritize hot hydrothermal synthesis is also consistent with the literature. Main corrections are rxn_008 and rxn_009 = mol_012 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002, rxn_010 = mol_013 + mol_007 + 4 mol_003 -> mol_015 + 2 mol_002 + mol_014, and rxn_011 = 2 mol_004 -> mol_005 + mol_003. Main scientific weaknesses are under-specified prebiotic hydrolysis of threonine aminonitrile, use of the non-prebiotic 'Biochemical' environment for neutral hydrolysis and peptide condensation, composite lumping in rxn_010, and lack of stereochemical annotation for threonine versus allothreonine. Overall this is a good network, but it falls short of approval because key hydrolysis and environment assignments remain under-defined.
